ai.description: *Spalerosophis arenarius* grows to 100–120 cm. It is yellowish-brown with reddish-brown dorsal spots and a distinct, dark, arrow-shaped head marking. It features a divided rostral scale.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Spalerosophis arenarius* is best distinguished by its single, enlarged, shield-like scale on the snout (rostral scale) that is surrounded by smaller, fragmented scales.
ai.habitat: The Red Spotted Royal Snake inhabits arid, sandy deserts and semi-arid scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Red Spotted Royal Snake is primarily crepuscular, actively foraging for small rodents and lizards during the cooler twilight hours to avoid the desert heat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Spalerosophis arenarius* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the spring and summer months in its Indian range.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Spalerosophis arenarius* is found in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically across Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically inhabiting sandy desert environments.
